features.title: 2. Basic Setup (Line-by-Line)
description: Let's break down a basic implementation line by line.
1. First, we initialize our Fastify application.
2. Next, we register the `@ananay-nag/fastify-socket-io` plugin. You can pass any standard Socket.IO server options here (like CORS rules).
3. The `connectionHandler` is a custom hook provided by this plugin. It automatically fires the moment a new client connects, giving you direct access to the `socket` object.

4. Finally, we start the Fastify server. The plugin automatically hooks into Fastify's lifecycle, meaning when Fastify shuts down gracefully, your Socket.IO server will gracefully terminate all connections too.

features.title: 3. Advanced: JWT Authentication Hook
description: In production environments, you cannot trust anonymous socket connections. This plugin features a native, zero-friction integration with `@fastify/jwt`.
By setting `jwtAuth: true`, the plugin injects a global Socket.IO middleware that runs before the `connectionHandler`.
Line-by-line flow:
1. The client attempts a WebSocket handshake, passing a token via `auth.token` or the `Authorization: Bearer` header.
2. The plugin intercepts the handshake and extracts the token.
3. It uses your existing `fastify.jwt` instance to verify the signature.
4. If valid, the decoded payload is securely attached to `socket.data.user`, allowing you to instantly know exactly who is communicating without doing manual database lookups in your event listeners.

features.title: 4. Resilient Connection State Recovery
description: Mobile networks drop. Wi-Fi connections stutter. Connection State Recovery ensures your users don't lose data during transient disconnects.

When enabled, the server temporarily buffers events sent to a client while disconnected. If the client reconnects within the timeout window, the server automatically resends the buffered events and restores their room memberships.
This happens natively in memory without requiring an external Redis adapter, making it perfect for single-instance Node.js deployments.

features.title: 5. Strongly Typed Events (TypeScript)
description: For enterprise teams, type safety is non-negotiable. Our plugin natively exports a generic wrapper to strongly type your entire real-time architecture.
1. `ClientToServerEvents`: Defines what the server is allowed to listen for (`socket.on`).
2. `ServerToClientEvents`: Defines what the server is allowed to emit (`socket.emit`).
3. `InterServerEvents`: Defines events sent between multiple server instances.
4. `SocketData`: Strictly defines the shape of `socket.data` (e.g., your JWT user payload).
Once registered with these generics, your IDE will provide auto-complete for event names and throw compiler errors if you attempt to emit invalid payloads.

features.title: 6. Live Demo Integration
